author: iFixit
description:
The ASUS ROG Flow Z13 carries an eye-popping 10 out of 10 repairability score in France. But does this $2,000 gaming tablet-laptop hybrid really deserve a perfect score?

We tore down the ROG Flow Z13 and scored it using iFixit's own repairability criteria. There's plenty to like: an easily removable display, a screwed-in battery, accessible M.2 storage, modular components, and a published service manual. But soldered RAM, wireless hardware, ports, incomplete documentation, and limited parts availability tell a more complicated story.

The result? ASUS says 10/10. Our repairability engineers gave the ROG Flow Z13 a 7/10.

More importantly, this teardown raises a bigger question: As repairability scores become more common around the world, should manufacturers be allowed to self-report scores that consumers see on price tags?
